summary: Helwig Schmidt-Glintzer is a scholar of sinology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Göttingen (1967–1968) and the University of Munich (1968–1973), later holding academic posts at Munich (~1982–1993) and Göttingen (~1993–2015).

Hemchandra Raychaudhuri was an Indologist and historian who taught Jitendra Nath Banerjea. He served at the University of Calcutta as Carmichael Professor and Head of Ancient Indian History and Culture (attested 1939, 1965) and of History (attested 1965).
Hemmige Shriniwasrangachar Biligiri is a linguist and Indologist. His career includes serving as a professor at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, attested in 1991 and 2026.

Hendrik Arent Hamaker was a scholar of linguistics who studied at Athenaeum Illustre of Amsterdam (~1804–1807). He was Professor of Arabic, Chaldaean, and Syriac at Franeker (1815–1817) and Professor of Arabic at Leiden (1817, 1822–1835).
Hendrik van Gelder was a historian and archaeologist. He held academic positions at Utrecht University from 1906 to 1915 and subsequently at Leiden University from 1915 until 1921.

Henepola Gunaratana is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Vidyasekhara Pirivena, Buddhist Missionary College, Kelaniya, and American University (BA 1975, PhD ~1980). He held posts at American University, Georgetown, Bucknell, and Maryland.

Heng Sure is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Oakland University, UC Berkeley, and the Graduate Theological Union (PhD 2003 under Ronald Y. Nakasone and Hsuan Hua). He held professorships at Bond University, GTU, and Dharma Realm Buddhist University.
Heng Yin works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned a doctorate at Yunnan University (2018–2025) and was appointed assistant professor at China West Normal University in 2023.

Henk Blezer works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Leiden University (1987–1997), where he also served as a postdoctoral researcher (1993–1997) and lecturer (2002–2008), alongside a post at the International Institute for Asian Studies (1997–2001).

Henk Bodewitz was an Indologist who completed his degrees and PhD under Jan Gonda at Utrecht University (~1956–1973). He held posts at Utrecht (1966, 1976–1992 as chair of Sanskrit) and Leiden University (~1972–1976, 1992–2002).

Henri Arvon was a philosopher and scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Strasbourg. He taught at Prytanée National Militaire, the University of Clermont-Ferrand (1966–1971), and Paris Nanterre University (~1971–1982).

Henri Bergson was a French philosopher who studied at Lycée Condorcet, École Normale Supérieure (~1878–1881), and the University of Paris (~1888–1889). His career included teaching posts at Lycée David d'Angers (~1881–1883) and Collège de France (1900–1904).
Henri Cordier was a scholar of sinology and history who studied at Lycée Chaptal. He held posts at the Royal Asiatic Society North China Branch (1871), Sciences Po (~1886–1925), and INALCO (1888).

Henri Deydier was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Jean Przyluski, Henri Maspero, and Alfred Foucher, completed a diploma at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1946–1950), and joined the École française d'Extrême-Orient in 1950.

Henri Frei was a linguist and Japanologist. He studied at INALCO and the University of Geneva (PhD under Charles Bally), later holding posts at Peking University (1933–1934), Maison Franco-Japonaise (~1934–1938), and Geneva (1940–1969).

Henri Gaidoz was a linguist and religious studies scholar educated at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and under Albrecht Weber. He held posts at École Libre des Sciences Politiques (1872–1908) and École Pratique des Hautes Études (from 1876).

Henri Hauvette was an academic who studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand. He held posts at Grenoble Alpes University from approximately 1895 to 1910 and at the University of Paris from approximately 1910 to 1935.

Henri Hubert was a scholar of religious studies and archaeology. Educated at ENS and EPHE under Sylvain Lévi, he held posts at the National Archaeological Museum (~1898–1927), École du Louvre (1906), and EPHE (1907).

Henri Maspero was a sinologist and linguist who studied under Édouard Chavannes and Sylvain Lévi. He held posts at EFEO (1908–1920), Collège de France (1919–1944), Sorbonne/University of Paris (~1934–1944), and École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1934–1944).

Henri Massé was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and linguist. He held academic posts at the University of Algiers (~1916–1927) and the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (~1927–1958).
